record.original_question: Given a color-critical graph F with chromatic number chi(F) = r + 1, determine the F-free graphs with m edges that attain the maximum spectral radius.

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Given a color-critical graph F with chi(F) = r + 1, determine the graphs that attain the maximum spectral radius among all F-free graphs with m edges.
Recently, Li, Liu and Zhang [22] solved Problem 12 by showing the following nice result.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let r ≥ 2 be an integer and let F be a color-critical graph with chromatic number χ(F) = r+1; that is, F contains an edge e such that χ(F − e) = r. For an integer m ≥ 1, let G(m, F) denote the family of F-free simple graphs with exactly m edges (and no isolated vertices). The spectral radius λ(G) of a graph G is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

Determine, for all sufficiently large m, the graphs in G(m, F) that maximize λ(G), i.e., characterize the extremal graph(s) attaining
   max { λ(G) : G is F-free with m edges }.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved by Li, Liu, and Zhang, who characterized the F-free graphs of given size m with maximum spectral radius when F is color-critical with χ(F)=r+1, generalizing Nikiforov-type spectral Turán results. Related work on spectral Turán problems for color-critical graphs (e.g., books, theta graphs, cliques) supports this resolution.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Spectral Graph Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses spectral extremal problems for F-free graphs with given size and color-critical forbidden subgraphs.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of determining maximum spectral radius among F-free graphs with m edges for color-critical F is a stated problem in this area.

status_evidence.title: A strengthening of the spectral chromatic critical edge theorem: Books and theta graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes spectral extremal results for color-critical graphs with given size.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work by Li, Liu and Zhang extends and resolves the general color-critical case for fixed m.
